question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Over your shoulder.,b:Toward the right edge of the road ahead.,c:Directly at the oncoming headlights.
note: If oncoming drivers do not dim lights, keep your eyes on the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by glare.

question: Which is the best way to prevent alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Call a taxi.,b:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,c:Simply say
note: The only reliable way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive; alcohol impairs judgment and makes safe decisions harder after drinking.

question: What is the safest practice for children riding in a vehicle?
options: a:They may be held by a strong adult,b:They may stand in the back of the vehicle,c:They must be properly restrained in appropriate child seats or seat belts
note: Children must be secured in appropriate child restraints or seat belts; never hold a child in your arms while the vehicle is moving.

question: What color pavement markings separate lanes traveling in opposite directions?
options: a:White,b:Yellow,c:Red,d:Brown
note: Yellow lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate same-direction lanes.

question: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle you borrowed, what should you do?
options: a:Familiarize yourself with controls and check for defects,b:Hide defects so the owner isn't embarrassed,c:Assume it's the same as your car,d:Drive carefully without checking
note: When driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to locate and test controls and correct any defects before driving.

question: When stopped in a travel lane on the roadway, what is allowed?
options: a:You may stop to drop off passengers.,b:You may not stop in a travel lane for any reason.,c:You may stop to look up an address briefly.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane; proceed to a safe area off the roadway to pull over. If you miss an exit, go to the next exit to turn around.

question: If an approaching train is near enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Cross at your own risk if no signals are present.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
note: If a train is approaching and could be dangerous, you must wait until it has passed before crossing the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and wait for a flashing green light.,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, look both ways, and go only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly and expect approaching vehicles to yield.,b:Sound your horn to warn pedestrians and vehicles.,c:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and cross the sidewalk area only when safe.

question: What should a driver do when encountering a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Slow to a stop unless already in the intersection.,c:Continue as they have the right-of-way.
note: A steady yellow light warns that a red light is about to appear; stop unless you are already within the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:Drivers should use hand motions to decide,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left
note: If two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right.

question: Which behavior can be a sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Maintaining perfect lane position.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Driving more slowly than the flow of traffic.
note: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, erratic speed changes, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, liquor) change how alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Only mixed drinks cause strong effects,b:Yes — beer impairs less than wine,c:Yes — wine impairs less than beer,d:No — impairment depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream
note: All alcoholic beverages contain alcohol and will impair reflexes and judgment in proportion to the amount consumed.

question: When parallel parking, how close should your vehicle be to the curb?
options: a:Within 18 inches of the curb.,b:Within 12 inches of the curb.,c:Within 24 inches of the curb.
note: When parallel parked, position your wheels within 12 inches of the curb unless signs or markings indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Michigan law, who must wear a seat belt?
options: a:The driver, any front-seat passenger, and any child under age 16,b:Only the driver,c:Only passengers in the back seat,d:Only children under 8
note: Michigan law requires the driver, front-seat passengers, and children under 16 to be properly restrained.

question: Which factor does not affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle weight, brake condition, tires, roadway and weather; time of day does not directly affect stopping distance.

question: When are seat belts most effective?
options: a:When worn by the person driving the car.,b:When used only on expressways.,c:When worn by all occupants of the vehicle.
note: Seat belts protect everyone inside a vehicle; all occupants should wear them at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb is:
options: a:A good driving habit and required by law.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Necessary only during the maneuver itself.
note: You must signal in advance of lane changes or turns (at least 100 feet) to inform others of your intentions.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:To warn another road user — for example, if a child is about to run into the street.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:When passing a bicyclist.
note: Use your horn as a warning to others when they may not see you and a collision is possible, such as a child stepping into the street.

question: What is the most important speed management rule when approaching curves?
options: a:Accelerate gently before entering the curve.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Drive at the posted speed limit entering the curve and slow at the sharpest part.
note: Because of inertia, you should reduce speed before a curve to maintain control through the turn.

question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?
options: a:Honk to alert the bicyclist,b:Drive briefly in the bicycle lane to pass,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible
note: Slow and give bicyclists plenty of room when passing; do not crowd or create wind blast that could unbalance them.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates.,b:Not all crossings have flashing lights or gates.,c:All of the above.
note: Do not drive around lowered gates; many crossings lack gates or lights—obey signs and any flaggers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:May force their way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:Has the right-of-way.
note: When entering from a private driveway or road, yield to traffic on the public road and merge safely.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Use four-way flashers while driving,b:Turn on your headlights (use low beams when near other vehicles),c:Use your parking lights only
note: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days and use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season,b:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe,c:Checking antifreeze and windshield washer fluid is especially important in winter
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, ice, or similar hazardous winter conditions. Winter driving demands extra caution; check fluids and consider snow tires to improve traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may not pass from either direction.,c:Drivers in either direction may pass when it is safe.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposite-direction traffic and permits passing when safe.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:No turn allowed,b:Continue as if the light is green,c:Slow and prepare to stop if safe,d:You may immediately turn left after yielding
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the signal is changing to red; you should stop if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who yields?
options: a:The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right and proceed when safe.

question: Which of these can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Speeding up to avoid slow drivers.,b:Allowing extra travel time.,c:Turning off your signals.
note: Planning extra time for trips reduces stress and helps prevent aggressive driving; also obey traffic laws and use signals.

question: If you stop along the road at night, which lights should you leave on?
options: a:Headlights (low beams) and emergency flashers,b:All lights off,c:Parking lights only,d:High beams only
note: If you stop at night, leave your low beam headlights on and use emergency flashers so others can see your vehicle.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Accelerate to stabilize the car.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly
note: Keep control, steer straight, let the vehicle slow gradually, then brake gently and pull off when safe.

question: What should drivers do in bad weather regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Increase their speed to get through quickly.,c:Decrease their following distance.
note: In adverse weather, increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead to give more time to react.

question: What does a single dashed white line separating lanes mean?
options: a:Drivers may change lanes or pass when it is safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass under any circumstances.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass if safe.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn them to the left.,b:Turn them toward the curb (to the right).,c:Keep them straight ahead.
note: Turn the wheels toward the curb when parked downhill so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped) in fog because high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility further.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do about signaling?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Signal at least 500 feet in residential areas.,c:Signal before changing lanes and check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder.
note: Signal in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas) and check mirrors and blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: Why should you avoid following other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,b:You may not see the road between the cars.,c:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows suddenly.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance gives you time to react and stop to avoid a rear-end collision.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what action should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn to alert other drivers.,b:Slam on your brakes immediately.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers
note: If the accelerator sticks, turn on hazard lights, apply brakes, shift to neutral, and turn off the ignition only when safe to avoid locking the steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in platted subdivisions?
options: a:35 mph.,b:45 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: Platted residential subdivision speed limits are typically 25 mph unless posted otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?
options: a:On the main road just before the exit lane.,b:Only when you see a toll booth.,c:After you have moved into the exit lane.
note: Do not slow on the main road before the exit lane; move into the exit lane first, then slow down in the deceleration area.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do to warn other drivers?
options: a:Sound your horn at passing motorists.,b:Use your four-way (hazard) flashers and get off the road if possible.,c:Sit in the vehicle and wait quietly.
note: If disabled on a highway, signal, move off the roadway if possible, turn on hazard flashers, and lift the hood to warn other drivers.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive,b:Drive immediately to get it over with,c:Assume you will drive no differently
note: Emotional distress can impair your driving. Take time to calm and refocus before getting behind the wheel.

question: If involved in an accident, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Not stop,b:Stand in a traffic lane to direct traffic.,c:Stop at or near the scene and avoid standing in traffic lanes.
note: You must stop at or near the accident scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, do not stand in lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through a symbol indicates what?
options: a:Drivers should come to a complete stop,b:That some drivers should yield to other drivers,c:That action is forbidden
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol indicates the depicted action is prohibited.

question: Which of the following is true about emergency vehicles?
options: a:They have the right-of-way when using sirens and flashing lights.,b:They may not use loudspeakers to give instructions.,c:You should follow them closely to get out of the way faster.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens and obey any instructions from their loudspeakers; do not follow closely behind.

question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on a multi-lane roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if safe,b:Always keep your current speed,c:Honk at incoming drivers,d:Stop on the shoulder
note: On multi-lane roads, move over or adjust speed to allow vehicles to merge safely; if no vehicle beside you, consider moving over one lane.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Continue normally at posted speed.
note: A flashing yellow light signals caution: slow down, look, and proceed carefully if it is safe.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is operating nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way,b:Stop and block its path,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel
note: Yield the right-of-way by pulling to the curb or side of the road when safe to do so so emergency vehicles can pass quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection stop working because of a power outage, how should drivers proceed?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield in turn,b:Park and wait for the power to be restored,c:Turn on hazard lights and proceed without stopping
note: When signals are not functioning, drivers should yield as they would at a four-way stop: the vehicle that arrives first goes first; proceed with caution when it is your turn.

question: What is the “No zone” in relation to large trucks?
options: a:An area where loud stereos are not allowed,b:The blind spots around a truck or bus,c:A special reduced speed zone
note: The “No zone” refers to the truck’s blind spots on the sides, rear, and front where smaller vehicles disappear from view.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, which steering action is correct?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight at all times.,b:Turn the wheel opposite the direction you want to go.,c:Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: Steer into the skid (in the direction you want to travel); as control returns, correct the steering.

question: Which practice helps prevent crashes by reducing misunderstandings with other road users?
options: a:Ignore other drivers.,b:Drive only on side streets.,c:Communicate your intentions to other road users.
note: Signal changes, use lights, and use the horn when appropriate to let others know your intentions.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn to warn others?
options: a:When passing another car on the road.,b:As a substitute for braking.,c:If another vehicle is in danger of hitting you.
note: Use your horn to alert others to immediate danger or to avoid a collision.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you return?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder and wait for help.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.,c:Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
note: Reduce speed without heavy braking, then carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Only buses may use the lane,b:Drivers may optionally make that movement,c:Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown,d:Drivers must stop before making that movement
note: A pavement arrow mandates that drivers in the lane must make the movement indicated, following any other traffic controls.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you signal under normal driving conditions?
options: a:20 feet before the turn,b:As soon as you see the turn,c:At least 100 feet before the turn,d:50 feet before the turn
note: In normal conditions you should signal at least 100 feet before making a turn or lane change.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who does not obey traffic laws?
options: a:They are exempt from traffic laws,b:They can be ticketed,c:They will always receive only a warning
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motorists and may be cited for violating traffic laws.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice when reaching a street or crosswalk?
options: a:Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop
note: Do not step into a street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching and it appears they cannot safely stop; watch for driver actions before proceeding.

question: What practice best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors only after starting to back up,b:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse,c:Walk behind the vehicle and check before getting into the driver’s seat
note: Before backing, walk around the vehicle to check for children, pets, or objects you might not see from the driver’s seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left you should always do which of the following?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Swing to the right side of your lane.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,c:Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
note: Never back up or make a U-turn on a freeway; proceed to the next exit and safely turn around there.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on your windshield wipers.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Turning on your headlights.
note: Reducing speed should be your initial response to decreased visibility or hazardous conditions; then use lights and wipers as appropriate.

question: What is the most common color for general warning signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or text to alert drivers to hazards.

question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must be obeyed?
options: a:Blue.,b:Green.,c:White.
note: Regulatory signs (speed limits, no-turn, etc.) are typically white with black markings and are enforceable.

question: When changing lanes, what steps should you take?
options: a:Check only mirrors and then change,b:Only signal and change lanes quickly,c:Speed up and move over without signaling,d:Signal
note: Before changing lanes, signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear.

question: When is cruise control appropriate to use?
options: a:When driving in heavy traffic.,b:When driving in rural areas with light traffic.,c:When roads are slippery from rain or snow.
note: Cruise control is suitable on open, dry roads with light traffic—not in heavy or slippery conditions.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Split the difference and pass between both hazards.,b:Let the oncoming car pass first,c:Pull onto the shoulder between them.
note: When facing multiple hazards, deal with one at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then safely pass the bicyclist.

question: How is distracted driving best characterized?
options: a:Nothing to be concerned about,b:Extremely risky behavior,c:Very uncommon
note: Distracted driving is very risky and increases the chance of collisions with other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, you should remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Need less time to pass on downgrades.,b:Require a smaller turning radius.,c:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks require longer stopping distances than passenger vehicles.

question: What is true about driving on a wet roadway?
options: a:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires,c:As speed increases
note: At higher speeds, tires are less effective at wiping water away, increasing the risk of hydroplaning; slower speeds are safer on wet roads.

question: Orange-colored road signs typically indicate what?
options: a:Work zones.,b:Regulatory requirements.,c:School zones.
note: Orange signs are used to warn about highway work zones and the presence of workers or equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you encounter an intersection that is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you,c:Proceed slowly into the intersection until traffic clears
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it without stopping; blocking the intersection is prohibited and unsafe.

question: During normal weather and traffic conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:One second,b:Two seconds,c:Three to four seconds
note: Keep a minimum following distance of three to four seconds in normal conditions; increase it during bad weather or heavy traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage, alley, or driveway.,b:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:Only when signs indicate.
note: You must yield to drivers on the public road when entering from a driveway, alley, or garage and to pedestrians on sidewalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but no stop line or crosswalk is marked, where should you stop?
options: a:At least 200 feet from either side,b:At the curb,c:Where you can see clearly without entering the intersection,d:Anywhere convenient
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

question: Is it acceptable to park in an access aisle next to a disability parking space?
options: a:When you have a disability placard.,b:When all other spaces are full.,c:No — under no circumstances.
note: Access aisles must remain clear for mobility access; parking in them is prohibited and is a traffic infraction.

question: Hydroplaning is most often caused by which of the following?
options: a:Sudden stops,b:Sudden turns,c:Driving too fast for wet conditions so tires cannot clear water
note: At higher speeds, tires may be unable to clear water from the road and can lose contact with the pavement, causing hydroplaning.

question: If you are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane is clear,b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning,c:Wave for an oncoming driver to let you go
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and it is safe to complete the turn.

question: What hazards do worn or bald tires present?
options: a:They can make turning more difficult,b:They are more likely to hydroplane,c:They can increase your stopping distance
note: Tires with insufficient tread increase stopping distance, reduce traction, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which actions should you take?
options: a:Signal only if traffic is present.,b:Change lanes quickly without checking.,c:Signal
note: Proper lane change: signal early, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: How should a seat belt be positioned to be effective?
options: a:Hidden beneath the seat.,b:Kept loose for comfort.,c:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
note: Lap belts should fit low across the hips and shoulder belts should lie comfortably across the chest to protect occupants.

question: What danger can a leaking exhaust system cause?
options: a:Excessive oil use,b:Carbon monoxide poisoning that can make you drowsy or cause death,c:Better fuel efficiency,d:Earlier tune-ups needed
note: A leaking exhaust can allow toxic fumes into the vehicle, causing drowsiness or death; have leaks repaired immediately.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Use the outside rearview mirror only.,b:Use the inside rearview mirror only.,c:Turn your head to look over your shoulder to check blind spots in addition to mirrors.
note: Mirrors do not show everything; always turn your head and check blind spots before every lane change.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for vehicles in the blind spot,b:Check only your side-view mirror,c:Check side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder for blind-spot checks
note: Before moving into another lane, check side and rearview mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.

question: Why should you be extra cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Bicycles must stay to the far right and not swerve.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you as you move out to pass.
note: Bicyclists may swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming traffic may not expect you to pull out to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:Green arrow pointing left,b:Solid green light,c:Flashing yellow light,d:Red arrow
note: A steady green arrow gives you the right-of-way to turn in the arrow's direction; oncoming traffic must stop for turning traffic.

question: What risk do drivers who eat or drink while driving face?
options: a:They have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.,b:They make no driving errors.,c:They are better drivers because they aren't hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving requires removing hands and eyes from driving tasks, making lane control and vehicle control more difficult.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you legally required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At a stop sign, a red light, or when directed by a traffic officer,b:Only at stop signs,c:Only when a police officer signals you,d:Only when other vehicles are present
note: You must stop at stop signs, red signals, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a driver of a small vehicle be prepared for?
options: a:Wind gusts that can affect vehicle control,b:Loud music from the large vehicle,c:Lower fuel efficiency,d:Extra lighting glare
note: Large vehicles can create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles; be prepared to correct steering when passing.

question: What does a flashing red light at an intersection mean?
options: a:You do not have to stop completely.,b:The traffic signal is broken.,c:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding when safe.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when is it safe to proceed?
options: a:Go through as soon as the first train passes,b:Start across after watching the first track,c:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks
note: After a train passes, do not proceed until you can see clearly down all tracks. A second train may be approaching on another track.

question: What should you do when driving to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Depend entirely on road signs to find your way.,b:Only have a general idea of your destination.,c:Plan your trip in advance.
note: Before going into unfamiliar areas, plan your route using maps or directions so you avoid last-minute maneuvers and confusion.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights,b:Low beam headlights,c:Interior dome light,d:Parking lights only
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow to get better illumination without glare.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, under which condition must you always stop?
options: a:If a crossing gate is lowered,b:If the crossing lights are flashing,c:If a stop sign is posted
note: Stop when gates are lowered, red lights flash, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals, or a train is visible or so close that continuing would be hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on green, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain normal speed without checking,b:Stop unless a sign says otherwise,c:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection,d:Turn wide into other lanes
note: You may turn on a steady green unless prohibited, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the centerline has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is on your side, you may:
options: a:Pass only on expressways.,b:Pass when the way ahead is clear.,c:Only pass in an emergency.
note: If the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass by crossing the centerline when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: How does drinking alcohol while taking drugs typically affect you?
options: a:It decreases the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,b:It helps cure your illness.,c:It increases the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
note: Combining alcohol and drugs can increase their effects and make it more dangerous to operate a vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to make a left turn on a green light but heavy oncoming traffic is present. What should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection instead without entering the intersection.,b:Wait in the center of the intersection regardless of the light.,c:Enter the intersection to wait for a gap if the light is green and it's safe to prepare for the turn.
note: If the light is green and it is safe, you may enter the intersection to prepare for a left turn; yield to oncoming traffic and turn when clear.

question: When must you allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopped?
options: a:At a stop sign,b:At an intersection,c:When you are stopped on an uphill slope
note: Allow more space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope because the vehicle ahead could roll back when traffic moves again.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee to sober up.,b:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,c:Exercise.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not lower BAC.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pass as closely as possible,b:Slow and pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it,c:Ignore it and keep speed,d:Honk repeatedly
note: Be cautious when animals are on the road; pass slowly to avoid frightening them and creating a hazard.

question: On a two-lane street you're followed by a fire engine not using lights or siren. What should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Speed up to get out of the way.,c:Continue driving normally.
note: If an emergency vehicle behind you is not using lights or siren, you do not need to clear the path; continue normally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal only if other vehicles are present.,b:Signal only when driving at night.,c:Signal your intentions in advance.
note: Always use your signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling from a curb so other road users know your plans.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may proceed without stopping.,b:The driver on the right.,c:The driver on the left.
note: When two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on state highways?
options: a:25 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:35 mph.
note: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on state highways is 55 mph; follow posted limits where different.

question: An octagonal road sign always indicates what?
options: a:No parking,b:Speed limit,c:Stop,d:Yield
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop.

question: When may you drive across a dashed white line?
options: a:Any time without caution,b:When it is safe to change lanes,c:Only during daylight hours,d:Only when signaling
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Speed up to get through first.,c:Assume the other vehicle will stop.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way when vehicles arrive simultaneously.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:Left turns are prohibited,b:You may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You must stop completely before turning,d:You may turn without yielding
note: A flashing yellow arrow means left turns are permitted but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: Which parts of the road freeze first and dry last during cold weather?
options: a:Roads in the sun,b:Flat open areas,c:Sections shaded by trees or buildings
note: Shaded sections of the road can freeze sooner and remain icy longer than other areas; take extra care in shaded spots.

question: May you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Only if your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:No,c:If an approaching train is not too close.
note: Do not cross when gates are down or moving; flashing red lights and lowered gates require you to stop until the crossing is fully clear and gates are up.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign mean?
options: a:Warning of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:Alerting to school zones.,c:Indicating public recreational areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (usually yellow or orange) warn drivers of possible hazards or changing road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down before you enter the exit ramp,b:Keep your speed constant while on the exit ramp,c:Slow down once you have moved onto the exit ramp
note: Do not slow down on the freeway travel lanes; reduce your speed once you are on the exit ramp where it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Let it go and continue driving safely,b:Pull next to them and yell,c:Flash your high beams aggressively,d:Brake-check them
note: To avoid road rage and danger, do not respond aggressively if cut off; let it go and maintain safe driving behavior.

question: How should you check a blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Only check the rearview mirror.,b:Only check the side mirror.,c:Glance over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.
note: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in the blind spot before moving over.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Red lines.,b:White lines.,c:Yellow lines.
note: Yellow lines are used to divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: Which describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who daydreams or stares off the roadway while driving.,b:Someone who maintains eye contact with a passenger while driving.,c:Someone who watches only the vehicle directly ahead.
note: Distractions like daydreaming or looking away reduce situational awareness and increase crash risk.

question: Which factor(s) affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling,b:The condition of your brakes and tires,c:All of the above
note: Braking distance is influenced by vehicle speed, the condition of brakes and tires, and pavement conditions among other factors.

question: Which of these is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted,c:You become more alert
note: Alcohol impairs vision, judgment, reaction time, and alertness; it makes drivers less safe, not more alert.

question: How close to a railroad crossing are you allowed to park?
options: a:You may not park within 100 feet of a railroad crossing.,b:You may not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.,c:You may not park within 75 feet of a railroad crossing.
note: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing to ensure clear visibility and safe passage of trains.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time from different highways, who yields?
options: a:Either one may go first,b:The larger vehicle yields,c:The vehicle on the right yields,d:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right
note: When two vehicles reach an intersection simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: Which effect does alcohol have on drivers?
options: a:Slows reflexes and reaction time,b:Makes you more alert,c:Helps you sleep better while driving,d:Improves coordination
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, decreasing reaction time and impairing judgment needed for safe driving.

question: When roads are slippery, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Reduce your following distance,b:Ignore following distances,c:Increase your following distance,d:Keep the same distance as on dry roads
note: On slippery roads you need a greater distance to stop, so increase following distance to improve safety.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, how should you respond?
options: a:Call the police immediately from the roadway.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Flash your lights to signal they are wrong.
note: Remain calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way; trying to retaliate increases danger and escalation.

question: About how much alcohol does the average body eliminate per hour?
options: a:One standard drink per hour.,b:Two drinks per hour.,c:Three drinks per hour.
note: On average, the body processes about one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:Only a recommended driving speed.,c:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions require it.

question: Why must drivers exercise increased caution at night?
options: a:Traffic is denser at night,b:There is a larger volume of traffic at night,c:Visibility is reduced after dark
note: Because visibility is reduced after dark, drivers cannot see as well; headlights are required from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise or whenever persons or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: What should you do before changing lanes on a multilane highway?
options: a:Turn on your headlights,b:Sound your horn to alert other drivers,c:Check your mirrors and blind spot and then signal
note: Before changing lanes, check rearview and side mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot, then signal and change lanes when safe.

question: A speed advisory sign attached to a curve means what?
options: a:You may ignore it in bad weather,b:It is triangular,c:The recommended safe speed for the curve; reduce speed in wet/icy conditions,d:It is blue with black lettering
note: Advisory speed signs recommend a safe speed for the curve; drivers must use lower speeds in adverse conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you not pass other vehicles?
options: a:All of the above,b:When your view is blocked by a curve or hill,c:When school bus lights are flashing or at intersections,d:Before or on a railroad crossing
note: Do not pass in no-passing zones, at intersections, on hills or curves with limited visibility, at railroad crossings, or when a school bus is stopped with red lights.

question: Why is night driving generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more at night.,b:It is more likely to rain at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards and judge distances; use headlights and slow down.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked along the road, what should you assume?
options: a:The driver may open the car door or step out, so use extra caution.,b:That the driver will respect your right-of-way.,c:You should slam on your brakes.
note: Assume someone could exit the parked vehicle or a door could open; leave space and be cautious when passing.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines across traffic lanes) typically painted?
options: a:Next to churches and schools,b:In curves and on hills,c:At mailboxes,d:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks
note: Stop lines are painted across lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks to indicate where drivers must stop.

question: Why is it important to allow a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:To keep traffic moving faster.,b:To allow time to react to unexpected situations.,c:To prevent distractions.
note: A space cushion gives you time and room to respond to other drivers' mistakes or sudden hazards.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to cross because trains are unlikely,b:Dangerous and to be approached with caution,c:Safe places to park temporarily
note: Railroad crossings are potentially dangerous; always look and listen for trains and obey signs, signals, and flaggers.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,b:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to make sure the way is clear.,c:Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
note: Exit the vehicle and check behind it before backing up; do not rely solely on mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign and stop,b:Continue driving,c:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic
note: A flashing red light means stop; proceed only when it is safe to do so, just like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you proceed through an intersection controlled by a stop sign but with no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After signaling for a turn,b:After slowing down and checking for traffic,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection,d:After coming to a complete stop before entering and ensuring it is safe to proceed
note: Stop before entering the intersection where a stop sign is present; if no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering and proceed when safe.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Become better drivers because they are more careful.,c:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time; it is unsafe to drive after drinking.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane,b:Keep driving at the same speed,c:Pull to the right curb and stop until it passes
note: Immediately pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.

question: What should you do on slippery roads regarding speed?
options: a:Speed up to avoid skidding,b:Slow down below the posted limit if necessary,c:Drive the posted speed limit regardless,d:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of slippery conditions and avoid using cruise control; safety may require going below the posted limit.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:A person in a traffic study.,b:A blind person.,c:A deaf person.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When you see a police car,b:When entering a highway with other cars present,c:When conditions make driving less than perfect
note: Drive below the posted speed when roads are wet, visibility is poor, or anything makes conditions less than ideal for safe driving.

question: When passing a parked vehicle, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:To honk to alert drivers and pedestrians to your presence.,b:All other drivers to respect your right-of-way.,c:A person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
note: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars and be ready for someone to open a door or step into your path.

question: If you drink socially, what measure helps ensure safe travel home?
options: a:Take a cold shower before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Drink coffee before driving.
note: Arrange a sober ride home rather than relying on coffee or showers, which do not reduce BAC; on average the body needs about an hour to process one drink.

question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Ignore and maintain speed,b:Speed up to distance yourself,c:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass,d:Slam on your brakes to scare them
note: If someone is tailgating you, safely change lanes or gradually reduce speed to let them pass; do not brake-check or escalate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit,b:A speed that is safe for existing conditions,c:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent given weather, traffic, road, and visibility conditions; obey posted speed limits.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light indicates what?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Stop and wait for a green light
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing another vehicle unsafe and therefore prohibited?
options: a:When you have a clear view of the road ahead.,b:When next to a broken yellow line.,c:On a hill or curve with limited visibility.
note: Do not pass on hills or curves where you cannot see oncoming traffic or the road ahead clearly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed,c:Drive carefully through the intersection
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down and watch for cross-traffic before continuing.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you allow it?
options: a:The use of a complete lane.,b:To share only half a lane.,c:To drive on the shoulder beside you.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane and need room to maneuver safely.

question: What happens when you take drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,b:The combination increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It lessens alcohol's effects.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) increases impairment and crash risk.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They do not require extra space to turn,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles,c:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver
note: Large trucks have bigger blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop. Avoid lingering in a truck’s blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway, what is essential?
options: a:Ensure the passing lane is clear and signal before changing lanes.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Assume oncoming traffic will yield.
note: Only pass when the lane you want is clear and you have signaled; check mirrors and blind spots.

question: Which effects can alcohol have on a driver?
options: a:Impaired thinking ability and coordination.,b:Slowed reaction time.,c:False sense of confidence.
note: Alcohol dulls judgment, slows reactions, and impairs coordination and vision; it can produce false confidence.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how dangerous is night driving?
options: a:Only riskier in rural areas,b:Less dangerous,c:More dangerous because visibility is reduced and there may be more impaired or tired drivers,d:No more or less dangerous
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare, and a higher proportion of impaired or drowsy drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After completing a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:In the center of the street,b:In the right lane,c:Any lane is acceptable,d:In the left lane of the one-way street
note: When turning left from a two-way onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the left lane closest to the lane you left.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called what?
options: a:Information signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Warning signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions ahead and should be obeyed to avoid accidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection permit you to do?
options: a:Must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,c:Drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection when it is safe; yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What should you do to drive safely at night?
options: a:Not drive if you are tired.,b:Only drive with high beams on.,c:Increase your following distance and ensure headlights work properly.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance and make sure headlights are functioning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic light,b:Honk to get the officer's attention,c:Follow only traffic signs,d:Obey the officer's directions
note: When an officer is directing traffic, drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must follow the officer's directions rather than traffic signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow and proceed if no one else is coming,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching,c:Treat as a yield sign,d:Stop completely and proceed only when safe
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: come to a full stop, yield, and go when safe.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, which of the following occurs?
options: a:Your body metabolizes alcohol faster,b:You become more coordinated,c:You become less confident,d:Reaction times slow and errors increase
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, increases confidence but reduces judgment, and leads to more driving errors.

question: Which of these lowers the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Do not speed on wet roads.,b:All of the above.,c:Use tires with proper air pressure and good tread.
note: Avoiding excessive speed and maintaining proper tire pressure and tread depth all reduce hydroplaning risk.

question: When should drivers use the parking brake?
options: a:Only when parked in a driveway.,b:Only when parking on an incline.,c:Every time they park.
note: Always set the parking brake when parking, turn off the engine, take the keys, and lock the vehicle.

question: If your vehicle’s turn signals fail, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Your horn.,c:Hand signals.
note: Use standard hand signals when your vehicle’s turn signals are not functioning.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:When driving in daylight with good visibility.,b:On paved highways in good conditions.,c:On a wet or icy road.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, gravel, or otherwise slippery surfaces and in poor traction conditions.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Only if directed by a police officer.,b:Only if a train is visible from a distance.,c:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.
note: Stop when flashing red signals and gates are active or if directed by a flagger or stop sign; do not cross until signals stop and gates are fully raised.

question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On a hill.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: It is unlawful to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane; when parking on a street, stay within 12 inches of the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes from the right to the left on a multilane highway, what should you check?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights,b:Sound your horn,c:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot,d:Only look in your rearview mirror
note: Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear before changing lanes; signal as well.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach an intersection with a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red. What should you do?
options: a:Honk your horn and proceed.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection even if you have a green light; be extra cautious around pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When the car in front of you is disabled.,b:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,c:When turning left into a driveway.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes as long as you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

question: If another driver is aggressive toward you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash lights angrily,b:Cut them off to slow them down,c:Retaliate by tailgating,d:Avoid eye contact
note: If threatened by an aggressive driver, stay calm, slow down, let them pass, and avoid eye contact or gestures.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a vehicle entering your lane from an entrance ramp on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to pass them,b:Honk so they will yield,c:Change lanes or slow to allow them room to merge
note: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway by changing lanes or reducing speed so they can merge safely.

question: How should you negotiate turns when the roads are slick?
options: a:Change lanes quickly,b:Accelerate rapidly through the turn,c:Take turns more slowly than usual
note: Approach turns and curves at slower speeds than normal in slippery conditions to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.,b:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,c:Ignore the guard and copy surrounding traffic.
note: Always be prepared to reduce speed and exercise caution when directed by a crossing guard, sign, or an officer; follow their instructions in school zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return immediately after passing.,b:When there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,c:Only if you plan to turn left.
note: After passing, return to the right lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is enough space.

question: What does a red arrow displayed on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or arrow appears,b:Stop then proceed when clear,c:Proceed slowly through the intersection
note: A red arrow requires a full stop and you must remain stopped until a green light or green arrow authorizes movement.

question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Merge to the right immediately.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and yielding to others, like a stop sign.

question: What helps conserve gasoline while driving?
options: a:Slowing down gradually to avoid unnecessary braking,b:Sitting in drive with the car running,c:Accelerating quickly from stops
note: Looking ahead and slowing gradually reduces the need for frequent acceleration and braking, which improves fuel efficiency.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:The same side as traffic is moving,b:The side with the lightest traffic,c:The side facing oncoming traffic
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and better avoid hazards.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers.,b:Human error.,c:Bad weather.
note: Most crashes occur due to human error, such as failing to see other vehicles or making unexpected moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection wanting to turn but are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,c:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
note: Do not make last-minute turns; continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always use your turn signal?
options: a:When changing lanes or pulling into traffic from a parking area or curb.,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Only during the maneuver itself.
note: You must signal each time you change lanes, pull into traffic, or leave a curbside parking space to inform other drivers of your intentions.

question: Which of these will sober a person who has been drinking?
options: a:Tomato juice and lime.,b:Hot coffee.,c:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce impairment; remedies like coffee do not sober someone.

question: What does a 'No stopping' sign generally allow you to do?
options: a:Stop to discharge passengers at any time.,b:Stop long enough to unload packages.,c:Stop only to avoid a conflict with other traffic or obey a police officer or traffic signal.
note: 'No stopping' means you may only stop to obey traffic signals or police, or to avoid conflict with other traffic; you may not stop for convenience.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic signal at an intersection mean?
options: a:Yield to other cars.,b:Go.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow indicates the light is about to turn red; slow down and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and driving?
options: a:Safe after a few drinks,b:Only dangerous for inexperienced drivers,c:A serious traffic safety problem,d:A minor traffic safety problem
note: Driving under the influence is extremely dangerous; alcohol impairs the ability to drive safely regardless of experience.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the blind spot to prevent merging,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you,c:Keep a steady pace
note: Do not drive in someone else’s blind spot; either speed up or fall back so the other driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the minimum speed limit on freeways?
options: a:45 mph,b:55 mph,c:70 mph
note: Unless marked otherwise, the minimum speed limit on freeways is 55 mph. Always obey posted speed limits when different.

question: When you are being tailgated and there is an open right lane, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance to the tailgater,b:Slow down abruptly to encourage the tailgater to pass,c:Move over to the right if there is an open lane
note: If a right lane is available, move over to it. If not, wait until the road ahead is clear and then reduce speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly.

question: If you must stop quickly and your vehicle lacks ABS, what is the recommended braking method?
options: a:Firmly pump the brake pedal.,b:Hold down the brake pedal.,c:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.
note: Pumping the brakes helps stop a vehicle quickly while allowing you to maintain steering control when the vehicle does not have ABS.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Remain in your lane and maintain your slow speed.,b:Speed up slightly to delay other drivers.,c:Pull off the right side of the road and let the traffic pass.
note: When your slow driving causes backups, pull over where safe to let other vehicles pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Use your turn signal several seconds before the turn,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection,c:Turn the steering wheel immediately
note: Activate your turn signal three to four seconds before you begin your turn so other road users know your intentions.

question: What do speed limit signs communicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area.,b:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.,c:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.
note: Speed limit signs indicate the legal maximum (or minimum) speed under ideal conditions; you must slow down when conditions make it unsafe.

question: Which of the following should you do when changing lanes?
options: a:Avoid signaling your intentions.,b:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,c:Fail to check for other drivers.
note: When changing lanes you should check mirrors, signal, and verify the lane is clear.

question: What are regulatory, enforceable signs called?
options: a:Guide signs,b:Regulatory signs,c:Information signs,d:Warning signs
note: Regulatory signs direct traffic and must be obeyed; failure to comply can result in penalties.

question: What is the safest method before crossing a railroad track?
options: a:Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.,b:Listen,c:Cross quickly when you see a train approaching.
note: Always look and listen for trains from both directions and obey all signals; never cross until you are sure it is safe.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of these could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.
note: Any action that distracts your attention, eyes, or hands from driving increases crash risk.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where is the safest place to look?
options: a:At the approaching vehicle’s wheels,b:Toward the right side of the road,c:Toward the left side of the road
note: If another driver does not dim high beams, glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping enough view of the roadway.

question: What does a “No standing” sign mean at a certain location?
options: a:You may stop temporarily only to pick up or discharge passengers,b:You may never stop your vehicle there,c:You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle
note: A No Standing sign means stopping is allowed only briefly to load or unload passengers; parking is not permitted.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Get out and go for help on foot,b:Lie down in the snow,c:Stay in your car and wait for help,d:Walk into the road to flag vehicles
note: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your vehicle where you are more likely to be found and safer than walking in severe conditions.

question: What affects your ability to stop quickly?
options: a:Signal lights.,b:The time of day.,c:Road conditions like wet or slippery surfaces.
note: Stopping ability is greatly affected by road conditions; reduce speed when roads are slippery to maintain control.

question: You approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,b:Drive to the right and stop in the lane.,c:If possible
note: When approaching stopped emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicles with lights flashing, change lanes away if safe; otherwise slow down and give as much space as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which centerline pattern prohibits passing from either direction?
options: a:Solid white,b:Combination solid and broken yellow,c:Single broken yellow,d:Double solid yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-way road means neither direction may cross to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in the right lane of an expressway, when should you move into the left lane?
options: a:If traffic in your lane is slow and left lane is moving faster,b:Whenever you want to pass,c:During bad weather only,d:When you see an exit ahead
note: Move to another lane or adjust speed so you don't impede traffic and to allow others to merge when necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a right turn, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the center of the street,b:In the middle lane,c:Close to the left side of the street,d:As far to the right side of the road as possible
note: To make a right turn safely, move as far right as practicable before turning.

question: On potentially slippery roads, which of the following should you avoid?
options: a:Using cruise control,b:Reducing speed,c:Careful steering maneuvers,d:Increased following distance
note: Do not use cruise control on slippery roads; reduce speed and increase following distance instead.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is the hand signal indicating?
options: a:Come to a stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Turn left.
note: A raised left arm (hand up) means the driver intends to turn right; treat accordingly.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Allow extra following distance,b:All of the above,c:Approach other vehicles with caution,d:Keep windshield and mirrors clear
note: In sleet or snow you should clear windows and mirrors, increase following distance, and approach vehicles cautiously.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wearing your seat belt,b:Limiting driving to weekdays,c:Staying in the right lane on multilane highways
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective measure to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash.

question: Compared with smaller vehicles, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots; trucks and large SUVs have areas not visible in mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach an intersection and the light turns from green to yellow, what is the safest action?
options: a:Apply the brakes sharply to stop immediately.,b:Be prepared to stop before entering the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the light will soon turn red. Slow down and be prepared to stop if it is safe.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: come to a full stop, then proceed when safe.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that which steady light will appear next?
options: a:Steady green,b:Flashing yellow,c:Steady red
note: A steady yellow indicates the signal is about to change to a steady red; prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection.

question: Which of the following can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating,b:Changing a radio station or CD.,c:Talking or texting on a cellphone.
note: Drivers make many decisions per mile; performing additional tasks like eating, texting, or changing media creates dangerous distractions.

question: About how far could a fully loaded tractor-trailer travelling at 55 mph take to come to a complete stop?
options: a:About 125 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:Approximately 400 feet.
note: Large trucks require much more stopping distance—often up to roughly 400 feet at 55 mph.

question: How do you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Only look in your side mirrors,b:Turn your head and look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter,c:Use automatic sensors without head checks,d:Only look in your rearview mirror
note: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors; check by turning your head and looking over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:A pedestrian.,b:Another driver.,c:The funeral procession.
note: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists should yield the right-of-way to funeral processions; remaining vehicles in the procession may follow through intersections when the lead vehicle enters.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore it,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop,c:Turn on your hazard lights and continue,d:Speed up and exit the street
note: On a one-way street, you must drive toward the nearest roadside and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights or siren.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, what must you do?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road,c:Pull completely off the road and stop
note: On narrow roads, allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion so both vehicles can pass safely.

question: When meeting an oncoming car with blinding headlights, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road until the vehicle has passed.,b:Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.,c:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.
note: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on, avert your gaze to the right edge of your lane to avoid being blinded.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you turn right on a red light?
options: a:Before pedestrians have finished crossing the intersecting crosswalks.,b:Where there is a sign prohibiting right on red.,c:After coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.
note: You may turn right on red only after a full stop, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles, and if no sign prohibits the turn.

question: During very adverse conditions or higher speeds, what following distance should you keep?
options: a:Six or more seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Four seconds.
note: Increase your following distance to six or more seconds during poor weather, heavy traffic, or higher speeds to allow extra reaction time.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited for vehicles in both directions.

question: Consuming which types of substances may impair driving and lead to DUII?
options: a:Alcohol,b:Prescription drugs only,c:Alcoholic beverages only
note: Many substances—alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some legal medications—can impair driving and result in arrest for DUII.

question: If a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
options: a:Whoever started moving last,b:Whoever is slower,c:The driver making the turn
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the road, even when turning and even if the pedestrian is not in a marked crosswalk.

question: After a stressful or angering incident at work, what should you do before driving home?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down and cool off.,b:Play loud music to ignore your feelings.,c:Drive fast to relieve stress.
note: Driving while emotionally upset impairs judgment—pause to calm down before starting to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure to change lanes?
options: a:Signal and change lanes immediately to avoid traffic.,b:Check mirrors and signal,c:Signal
