note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear before moving.

question: What does a steady green arrow on a traffic signal allow you to do?
options: a:Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow regardless of pedestrians.,c:Stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding straight.
note: A steady green arrow permits the indicated turn; you must be in the proper lane and yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass another car at any time.,b:To turn left into a driveway or make a legal left turn.,c:To pass a slow-moving truck when safe.
note: You may cross double solid yellow lines only to turn left into or out of driveways, alleys, or make permitted left turns.

question: If two railroad tracks are side by side and one train passes, what should you do?
options: a:Always proceed after the first train passes,b:Always stop before crossing two tracks,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding
note: After one train passes, check the other track(s) for additional approaching trains before you cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you generally do?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp then enter slowly.,b:Accelerate to the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,c:Enter below the speed of highway traffic to be cautious.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed, signal, look for a gap, and merge safely.

question: If you are involved in a crash, what steps should you take?
options: a:Leave the scene and report later.,b:Continue driving if damage is minor.,c:Stop immediately
note: Stop, assist injured persons if you can do so safely, and contact police and emergency services as needed.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:You have the emergency brake on,b:You are slowing down or stopping,c:You are making a turn
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping; keep them in working order.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A solid red light.,c:A yield sign.
note: A red flashing light has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

question: If a transit vehicle signals that it is re-entering traffic after a stop, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to let them know you’re there.,b:Yield to the transit vehicle.,c:Move to the left lane immediately.
note: Yield to a transit vehicle signaling to re-enter traffic; slow down, change lanes if safe, or stop to allow it to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on freeways?
options: a:55 mph.,b:70 mph.,c:45 mph.
note: On Michigan freeways, the standard maximum speed is 70 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: How do smoking and preparing to smoke while driving affect you?
options: a:They do not affect driving abilities.,b:They help maintain driver alertness on long trips.,c:They are distracting activities that can take your hands or eyes off the road.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you by requiring you to look away or take hands off the wheel, creating dangerous situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, you should:
options: a:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,b:Treat it like a four-way stop.,c:Continue if the intersection is clear
note: With a steady green light, you may proceed but must yield to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection.

question: Which kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only recreational drugs like marijuana.,c:Prescription medications
note: Many medications—prescription, OTC, and illegal substances—can impair driving; check warning labels and consult your doctor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Back up on the shoulder,b:Make the turn quickly from your lane,c:Stop and ask for help,d:Continue to the next exit and turn around safely
note: If you miss your exit you should continue to the next exit or other safe location to turn around — do not back up on a freeway or shoulder.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, what does that indicate?
options: a:A construction area is approaching,b:An intersection is just ahead,c:The road will become narrower ahead
note: A slanted edge line toward the center indicates the road narrows ahead; edge lines mark the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder.

question: When you approach a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Honk before passing.,b:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Drive past if no children appear to be exiting.
note: When a school bus displays its stop arm and flashing lights, all nearby vehicles must stop until it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Just before changing lanes.,b:After you have already begun to pass.,c:Early enough for other drivers to notice your intention.
note: Signal in sufficient time so other drivers can see and understand your planned maneuver.

question: What do crossbuck signs mark?
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Railroad crossings.
note: Crossbuck signs indicate a railroad crossing; yield to trains and obey crossing control devices.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is the first thing you must do?
options: a:Call the police,b:Determine if anyone is injured,c:Stop your vehicle
note: If you are involved in a crash, stop your vehicle if possible and move it off the road if it is safe to do so. If anyone is injured, call 911. Serious crashes must be reported to law enforcement when there is injury, death, or significant property damage.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror.,b:Your steering wheel.,c:Your seat.
note: First adjust your seat so you can see clearly and reach controls; then adjust mirrors and steering wheel as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car whose driver honks first,b:The car approaching from the right,c:The car approaching from the left
note: At an uncontrolled intersection of two similar roads, yield to the vehicle approaching from your right.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, besides setting the parking brake, which way do you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the curb,b:Turn them to the left only,c:Turn them away from the curb,d:Keep them straight ahead
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if brakes fail.

question: If you hear a fire engine or other emergency vehicle approaching from behind, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and continue in your lane.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and keep driving.
note: You must pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

question: Round traffic signs are used to indicate what?
options: a:Stop signs ahead,b:No passing zones,c:School zones,d:Railroad crossings ahead
note: Round (circular) signs warn of railroad crossings and advise extra caution when approaching them.

question: How should drivers respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Increase their speed to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; slow down, look carefully, and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, you must do what to your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,c:Maintain your current speed.
note: Reduce speed when turning so you can maintain control, stay in your lane, and react to hazards.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Stop driving and rest,b:Get some coffee and keep driving,c:Open your window to stay awake
note: Drowsy driving is dangerous; if you become tired, stop driving and rest or find a safe place to sleep before continuing.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be reduced.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can enhance or unpredictably change effects, increasing impairment and danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrives first.,b:The driver who arrives last.,c:The driver who waves others through.
note: At four-way stops, the first vehicle to stop proceeds first; if two arrive together, the vehicle on the right goes first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting in an intersection to finish a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Pulse your brakes,b:Keep wheels turned left,c:Keep wheels straight,d:Keep wheels turned right
note: When waiting to complete a left turn, keep your wheels straight so if you're struck from behind you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from multilane one-way streets or highways, where should you start?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: To turn left from multilane one-way streets/highways, start from the left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the first thing you should do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Honk repeatedly.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal your intention; return to lane only when safe.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:Being angry while driving.,b:Being under the influence of alcohol.,c:Taking amphetamines.
note: Extended wakefulness impairs driving similar to alcohol; e.g., 18–24 hours awake approximates certain BAC effects.

question: How should you respond to a work-zone sign that says '45 mph where workers present'?
options: a:Drive at the usual speed unless workers are present; when workers are present, slow to 45 mph or lower.,b:Immediately slow to 45 mph whether workers are present or not.,c:Merge to the right lane and maintain speed.
note: In such zones, slow down to the advisory speed when workers are present and drive with extra caution.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in back of your vehicle.,b:Only in front of the vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: Maintain space on all sides of your vehicle to give time to react to hazards and avoid collisions.

question: Which driving method helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.,b:Engage four-wheel drive.,c:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.
note: When roads are snow-covered or icy, reducing speed and increasing following distance are the most important techniques for avoiding crashes.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct steering response?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.,b:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Overcorrect quickly to regain control.
note: If your vehicle skids, remain calm and steer in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding to regain control.

question: What do two solid yellow lines down the center of the roadway mean?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only when you are at the top of a hill.
note: Two solid yellow lines indicate no passing by traffic in either direction; they separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When driving in traffic, which practice is safest?
options: a:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit.,c:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Driving consistently with the flow of traffic (within legal limits) reduces the chance of collisions caused by speed differentials.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:The day after it rains,b:Only when it's cold,c:The first 10 to 15 minutes of the storm,d:After it has been raining for an hour
note: Pavement is often most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of rain because oil and residue rise to the surface.

question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the roadway?
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Continuously scan the entire road and roadsides.
note: Search for and identify potential problems early by scanning far ahead and across the entire roadway and its sides.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching a roundabout?
options: a:Slow down before entering.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Come to a complete stop before entering.
note: Approach a roundabout at a low speed and prepare to yield to traffic already in the circle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:By using the shoulder of the highway.,b:If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.,c:On a hill or in a curve
note: You may not pass on hills or curves where visibility is limited, never drive on the shoulder to pass, and never pass across solid yellow lines.

question: What should someone do before driving while taking a non-prescription drug?
options: a:Continue driving regardless of label warnings.,b:Drink alcohol with the medication.,c:Read the drug labels for warnings about driving.
note: Over-the-counter medications can impair driving. Check labels and ask a doctor or pharmacist if unsure about driving while taking a drug.

question: Pennant-shaped roadside signs are typically used to indicate what?
options: a:School zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs placed on the left side of a roadway warn drivers they are entering a no passing zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On hills and curves,b:Only at intersections,c:At railroad crossings only,d:Never prohibited
note: Passing is prohibited in locations such as hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where visibility or safety is compromised.

question: What do diamond-shaped yellow-and-black signs usually warn you about?
options: a:Conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Directions to cities and towns.,c:School zones only.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs indicate upcoming road conditions or hazards; they typically have black symbols on yellow backgrounds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in line at a stop sign and cross traffic is clear after the vehicles ahead move, what must you do?
options: a:May slowly roll past the stop sign.,b:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:May proceed without stopping again.
note: You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign or stop line and yield to traffic and pedestrians before moving forward; do not let pressure from traffic make you skip the stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a correct set of passing procedures?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes, check mirrors and blind spot, and return when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in the mirror.,b:Wait until you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your side mirror before returning.,c:Signal only while you are passing to alert other drivers.
note: When passing, always signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and only return to your lane when you can clearly see the passed vehicle’s front bumper or headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: Which practice reduces the risk of a rear-end collision?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops by letting your vehicle slow gradually and signaling.,b:Stop abruptly to surprise drivers behind you.,c:Weave between lanes to keep traffic flowing.
note: Smooth deceleration and signaling give drivers behind you time to react and reduce rear-end collisions.

question: What is the proper name for turning your head and checking blind spots before lane changes?
options: a:A bad driving habit,b:Checking your blind spot (a good driving habit),c:Mirroring,d:Unnecessary scanning
note: Turning your head to check blind spots before lane changes is a good driving habit; don't rely only on mirrors.

question: When another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam setting,b:Turn headlights off and use parking lights,c:High beam setting
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle; switch to low beams to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: Why must drivers be particularly alert to motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers,b:They are more difficult to see than cars,c:They rarely use headlights
note: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss in traffic or in blind spots; it can also be harder to judge their speed and distance.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on your brakes,b:Grip the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop,c:Keep driving normally
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually. Once you are moving very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and steer to a safe area off the road.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other road users allow for?
options: a:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.,c:The increased stopping distance required by the larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks require greater stopping distances; give them space and avoid positioning where the truck driver’s view is blocked.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with signals flashing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train.,c:Look for a train then speed up to clear the crossing.
note: If warning signals are flashing, stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until signals and gates indicate it is safe to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:The presence of a stop sign only.,b:Use of your turn signals.,c:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.
note: Crossing safely requires judging road and weather conditions plus gaps in oncoming traffic.

question: If you have a tire blowout, what should you do first?
options: a:Do not immediately use your brakes and gradually slow down.,b:Take your foot off the gas.,c:Gradually slow and pull off the road.
note: If you experience a blowout, ease off the gas and avoid immediately braking; slow down gradually, then gently apply brakes and pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane-marking allows you to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line on your side.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and can be crossed to pass when safe.

question: Which of the following is a possible effect of alcohol?
options: a:Improved coordination,b:Faster judgment,c:Loss of concentration
note: Alcohol impairs concentration, coordination, and judgment even at low levels of consumption.

question: When is parking on the freeway shoulder allowed?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:If you turn on your four-way flashers.
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in an emergency.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what actions should you take?
options: a:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition,b:Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself,c:Work harder to steer
note: Power steering loss requires more effort to steer. Slow down, signal, and drive carefully to a safe spot to stop and address the problem.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:Children will always wait at the curb.,b:Children will only play on sidewalks.,c:Children may run into the street without looking.
note: Expect unpredictable behavior from children and reduce speed accordingly to avoid collisions.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.,b:It decreases your chances of an accident.,c:It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
note: Emotional stress can reduce concentration and impair driving ability; avoid driving when emotionally unstable.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' and how does it occur?
options: a:A result of excessive sleep the night before driving.,b:A condition prevented by frequent rest stops.,c:A condition caused by staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning.
note: Staring ahead for long periods without scanning can make you zone out, reducing reaction ability—take breaks and scan.

question: What should you do when you see signs indicating a nearby railroad crossing?
options: a:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly.,b:Try to drive around a gate if it is descending.,c:Look and listen for trains
note: When signs warn of a railroad crossing, slow, look, listen, and be prepared to stop if needed.

question: Which restraints are most effective in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: Wearing both lap/shoulder belts and using airbags together provides the most protection in frontal crashes.

question: If your vehicle strikes an unattended parked car and you cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and accident details.,b:Drive away and report later.,c:Do nothing if no one saw it.
note: If you cannot find the owner, leave a written note with contact information and accident circumstances.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Ignore the flagger and copy other cars,b:Drive at normal speed,c:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be there,d:Follow the flagger's directions
note: Drivers must obey flaggers and posted instructions in construction zones; failure to do so is illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding can be safe in light traffic.,b:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Driving excessively slowly can disrupt traffic and create hazards; speeding also increases the risk and severity of crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Always come to a full stop before proceeding.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic already in the roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and yield to traffic and pedestrians in the roadway you are entering; stop if necessary to avoid a collision.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without signals, what should you do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop.,b:Assume all crossings have signals.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop; wait until trains have completely passed.

question: What obligation does a driver have when encountering pedestrians?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it,b:Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians,c:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of your vehicle before proceeding
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians even if they are not crossing legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn through the median,b:Go to the next exit,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit
note: If you miss your exit, continue to the next one. Do not stop, back up, cross medians, or make sudden lane changes to try to catch an exit.

question: How can you avoid collisions caused by blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head quickly to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk your horn right before changing lanes.
note: Before turning or changing lanes, glance over your shoulder toward the direction of the move to check the blind spot; don't rely on mirrors alone.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted and driving with one hand while talking, what should you do?
options: a:Attempt to pass immediately,b:Give extra following distance and be prepared for sudden moves,c:Follow their example,d:Tailgate to pressure them
note: Allow extra space and be prepared for errors when the driver ahead appears distracted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Many crashes are caused by drivers doing what?
options: a:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,b:Yielding the right-of-way appropriately.,c:Driving too fast for conditions.
note: A common cause of crashes is driving too fast for current road or weather conditions; always reduce speed when conditions are poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?
options: a:Maintain speed and proceed without checking.,b:Always come to a full stop regardless of traffic.,c:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to stop to avoid a crash.
note: At an intersection with no signs or signals, yield to vehicles from the right and be prepared to stop if needed to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a stop sign, after stopping you should look which way first?
options: a:Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters.,b:Move when the vehicle ahead moves.,c:Right
note: When stopped, look left first (vehicles from that side are nearer), then right, then left again before proceeding.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, how should you safely return to the road?
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator,b:Stop immediately on the shoulder and back onto the road,c:Accelerate and steer back quickly
note: Do not panic. Ease off the accelerator, hold the steering wheel steady, slow down, then when traffic permits gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: When you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Take the right-of-way immediately.,b:Pass quickly to avoid delay.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Yield to blind pedestrians and be prepared to stop to prevent injury.

question: Which behavior is characteristic of a good defensive driver?
options: a:Driving slowly at all times regardless of conditions.,b:Maintaining a constant speed on every road.,c:Looking out for the actions of other drivers and anticipating potential problems.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate others' actions and adjust to avoid conflicts and crashes.

question: When driving in rain, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rainy conditions, use your low beam headlights to increase visibility.

question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain the same speed and lane position without adjustment.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Slow down to allow space in front of your vehicle so they can pass safely.
note: Ease off the accelerator to create room for the passing vehicle to move back into your lane safely.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road signify?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass
note: Solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; they discourage or prohibit lane changes.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:The area visible in your rearview mirror.,b:The space directly behind your vehicle.,c:An area you cannot see without turning your head.
note: Blind spots are areas beside or behind your vehicle that are not visible in mirrors and require a head check.

question: Which item does NOT affect your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Body weight,b:Time between drinks,c:Amount drunk,d:Type of alcoholic beverage consumed
note: BAC depends on weight, amount consumed, and time, but not on the type of alcoholic beverage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop before entering any crosswalk.,b:Stop at the stop line.,c:Stop before entering the intersection.
note: A red traffic light requires you to stop before entering the intersection; also stop at any stop line or crosswalk if present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A two-lane road divided by a broken yellow centerline indicates what?
options: a:The road is one-way,b:The road is under repair,c:No passing allowed,d:Traffic travels in both directions
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; a broken line allows passing when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Use the shoulder to pass,b:Pass without signaling,c:Use the oncoming traffic lane only when it is safe and legal,d:Flash your lights at oncoming drivers
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires using the oncoming lane and only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect that may affect safety, you should:
options: a:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can afford to fix it.,b:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,c:Wait until the next inspection to fix it.
note: Any defect affecting safe operation should be corrected promptly, preferably before driving the vehicle.

question: When pedestrians are in crosswalks marked by two solid white lines, what must drivers do?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way.,b:No one has the right-of-way.,c:Give pedestrians the right-of-way.
note: Crosswalk markings indicate where pedestrians should cross; you must stop for and yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed,b:Under no circumstances,c:When the crossing lights have stopped flashing
note: You must never go around lowered crossing gates. Always stop when signals indicate an approaching train.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?
options: a:They are blind and need extra right-of-way consideration.,b:They are police officers.,c:They are deaf.
note: When encountering a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop to ensure their safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass on the right of another vehicle?
options: a:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,b:On a narrow bridge.,c:If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there's an available passing lane.
note: You may pass on the right when there is a proper passing lane or when a vehicle is waiting or turning left; never pass by driving off the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed,b:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot
note: On an interstate, always signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you look?
options: a:At the vehicle's lights,b:Toward the right side of the road,c:Down at the dash,d:Toward the centerline
note: If another vehicle is using high beams you should glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining course.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Decrease your speed to stay relaxed.,b:Turn up the radio volume to stay alert.,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.
note: Regular stops to rest and stretch help prevent drowsiness more effectively than stimulants like loud music.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around lowered gates.,b:Drive faster than the train.,c:Stop if a train is nearby.
note: Railroad warning signs mean a train may be near; be prepared to stop and never go around barriers.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:Always ensure all passengers are using the appropriate seat belt or child restraint,b:You should never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag,c:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant even in a low-speed crash
note: Always fasten your seat belt and ensure children are properly restrained; infants should not be placed in a front seat with an active passenger airbag.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line,b:Passing is prohibited from either side,c:Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line,d:Passing is allowed both directions
note: Where a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, vehicles next to the broken line may pass when safe.

question: When you hear the siren or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down but remain in your lane.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you on the left.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.
note: Immediately pull as far to the right as is safely possible and stop until the emergency vehicle passes; if in an intersection, clear it before stopping on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an expressway behind other vehicles, what is most important?
options: a:Match the speed and position to merge smoothly with traffic,b:Keep eyes on the vehicle directly behind you,c:Stay as close as possible to the car ahead,d:Stop at the end of the ramp if necessary
note: Adjust your speed and position to merge smoothly into the flow of traffic rather than following too closely or stopping.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and that work is underway.,b:It is summer.,c:You must stop immediately and back up.
note: Work zone signs (orange with black lettering) warn that work is being done; slow down and pay extra attention.

question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights?
options: a:Wait for a flagger's signal,b:Turn down your radio to listen for trains,c:Cross quickly,d:Proceed when you know no train is coming
note: Approach railroad crossings with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction.

question: What is the best general way to reduce your risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly maintained and slow down when roads are wet.,b:Use cruise control on wet roads.,c:Drive faster to get across puddles quickly.
note: Well-maintained tires and reduced speed in wet conditions lower the chance of hydroplaning.

question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, how should you adjust?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,b:Increase speed to maintain momentum.,c:Slow down and turn on headlights if visibility is reduced.
note: Reduce speed and use headlights in rain; if visibility is severely reduced, safely pull over and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which actions should drivers take when preparing to turn left?
options: a:Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.,b:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Move into the left lane before the intersection.
note: Signal 3–5 seconds before turning, check mirrors as you slow, move into the left lane if multilane, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and turn when your path is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:New tires,b:Night driving only,c:Slow speeds,d:High speeds
note: Higher speeds dramatically increase stopping distance and the severity of collisions.

question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you watch for before proceeding?
options: a:The bus driver waving you on.,b:Children waving to you before you go.,c:Children walking along the side of the road.
note: Always watch for children walking near the bus; proceed only when it is safe and the bus signals are retracted.

question: Which of these is true about drowsy drivers?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably keep them alert,b:They can drive poorly and appear intoxicated,c:Drinking coffee is a full remedy,d:They never exhibit signs of impairment
note: Drowsiness can impair driving similarly to alcohol; simple measures like windows or radio are not reliable fixes.

question: Which recommendation does not directly promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean,b:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle,c:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark
note: Keeping windows clean and avoiding heavily tinted windows improves visibility at night; while a flashlight can be useful, it does not directly improve driving visibility.

question: When using a roundabout, who must you yield to?
options: a:Entering traffic,b:Traffic already in the roundabout,c:Traffic to your left only,d:Pedestrians only
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to traffic already circulating in it, which travels counterclockwise around the center island.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Cross immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Yield to any approaching train and never cross unless there is room for your vehicle on the other side.,c:Always stop before crossing regardless of traffic.
note: Be ready to yield to trains and ensure your vehicle can clear the tracks; do not shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign indicates what type of message?
options: a:A school crossing sign,b:An interstate route marker,c:Warning about potential hazards
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert drivers to upcoming hazards or changes in road conditions.

question: When driving on major highways, what should you do to maintain safety?
options: a:Focus on one distant point to relax,b:Rely on cruise control at all times,c:Drive with a single hand on the wheel,d:Stay alert and keep your eyes moving
note: On highways you must remain alert, keep scanning the road, and be ready to react to hazards to avoid 'highway hypnosis.'

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:How much time passes between drinks (and all the above),b:The body weight of the individual,c:The amount of food in the stomach
note: BAC and alcohol effects are influenced by how much you drink, how quickly you drink, your body weight, and whether you have eaten, among other factors.

question: Which traffic signal requires a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A solid green light.
note: A flashing red signal is equivalent to a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

question: What is the correct way to back up a vehicle safely?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open the door and step out to check.
note: When backing, look over your shoulder through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: When may you cross solid yellow center lines?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction,b:Only when making a turn,c:At any time
note: Solid yellow lines generally separate traffic moving in opposite directions and should not be crossed except to make a permitted turn into or out of a driveway or side road.

question: When stopped in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals, what should you ensure?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:You have the right-of-way and don’t need to check for trains.,c:That there is enough room on the far side so you can completely clear the tracks.
note: Make sure you can fully clear the tracks before entering; never stop on the tracks or attempt to pass another vehicle while crossing.

question: Which driving adjustment is required when weather suddenly changes?
options: a:Ignore and continue as before,b:Only worry about vehicles behind you,c:A change in driving to adapt to new conditions
note: When weather changes, adjust speed, following distance, and other driving habits to match the new conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow and a red light simultaneously, what may you do?
options: a:Drive straight ahead only,b:Wait for a solid green light to go any direction,c:Proceed only in the direction of the green arrow
note: A green arrow with a red light authorizes movement only in the direction indicated by the arrow, as long as the intersection is clear.

question: Driving while distracted by any activity typically causes what effect?
options: a:You will react faster to hazards,b:You will react more slowly to hazards,c:You will drive faster than usual
note: Distractions slow reaction times and reduce attention to driving tasks, increasing crash risk.

question: Which action best helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure your tires have good tread and proper inflation.,b:Both ensure good tire condition and reduce speed when wet.,c:Reduce your speed when driving in heavy rain.
note: Good tire tread and proper inflation, plus reducing speed in wet conditions, reduce hydroplaning risk.

question: Regulatory signs are used to do what?
options: a:Warn of upcoming hazards in a diamond shape.,b:Indicate what a driver must or must not do.,c:Indicate places of interest.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers the laws and rules that must be followed, such as speed limits and turn prohibitions.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop no matter what.,b:Stop and drive toward the scene to get a better view.,c:Keep your attention on driving and continue unless you are involved or help has not arrived.
note: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived; keep moving and watch for people on or near the road.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the street under which circumstances?
options: a:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or against signals.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only when the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway regardless of how the pedestrian behaves.

question: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward is signaling what?
options: a:They intend to turn left,b:They intend to stop or slow,c:They are unsure,d:They intend to turn right
note: Left arm extended downward is the hand signal meaning the driver plans to stop or slow; adjust your driving accordingly.

question: If another vehicle is about to hit you, what should you do to alert them?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them.,b:Wave your arms wildly.,c:Turn off your lights.
note: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians to immediate danger when a collision is imminent.

question: When driving in fog, what headlight setting should you use and how should you proceed?
options: a:Use low beams, reduce speed, and drive cautiously,b:Use high beams to see farther ahead,c:Use parking lights only,d:Turn off lights to avoid glare
note: In fog you should use low beam headlights (not high beams) and reduce speed to improve visibility and safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which instruction must you obey over traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer directing traffic,c:A stop sign
note: Directions from traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings. Officers include police, fire police, flaggers, and school crossing guards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach an intersection and the light turns solid yellow. What should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately wherever you are.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and keep going.,c:Slow and stop before entering if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed carefully.
note: A solid yellow warns a red is coming; stop before entering if it is safe, otherwise proceed through the intersection carefully.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Flash your lights.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.
note: Always slow and be ready to stop for pedestrians, especially children; yield the right-of-way to those in crosswalks.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination can multiply impairing effects,b:The medicine will cancel the alcohol's effects,c:The alcohol reduces the medicine's power,d:Nothing — it's safe
note: Mixing alcohol with medications can greatly increase impairment and unpredictable effects; combining them multiplies risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate immediately,b:Ignore pedestrians,c:Back up to re-position,d:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection
note: A green light allows you to go, but you must first yield to any traffic or pedestrians still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a street with multiple lanes moving in your direction, into which lane should you enter?
options: a:Any lane marked with an arrow only,b:The far right lane always,c:The lane closest to the lane you came from,d:The middle lane
note: When turning onto a street with more than one lane going your direction, enter the lane nearest your previous lane and do not change lanes during the turn.

question: Guide signs that provide directional and mileage information have what background color?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: Guide or destination signs are green with white lettering and provide directional and mileage information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why is city driving considered more dangerous than expressway driving?
options: a:Because lanes are narrower,b:Because of lower speed limits,c:Because expressways are less maintained,d:Because of cross traffic and pedestrians
note: City driving has more intersections, cross traffic, and pedestrians, increasing the potential for collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic,b:Yield to traffic already on the interstate,c:Stop at the end of the ramp,d:Expect others to stop
note: When entering interstate traffic from a ramp, yield to vehicles already on the highway and merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign means what?
options: a:The sign is advisory only,b:You have ample time to slow down before the zone,c:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the sign,d:The reduced speed begins at the next speed sign
note: A posted reduced speed sign establishes the new speed limit starting at the sign; you must reduce to that speed at the sign.

question: How does even a small amount of alcohol affect your driving?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can impair you.,b:Alcohol does not affect driving skills.,c:Even small amounts reduce concentration
note: Any alcohol impairs the skills needed for safe driving—no amount of alcohol makes driving safer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Only stop if another vehicle is present.,b:Stop at the intersection,c:Slow down and proceed if the way appears clear.
note: A flashing red signal is equivalent to a stop sign: stop completely and go only when the intersection is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, which driver must yield?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, yield to that vehicle; proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless which condition is met?
options: a:Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.,b:You are able to clearly see the road ahead.,c:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
note: Safe passing requires you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane before encountering oncoming traffic, along with adequate visibility and speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line beside your lane means passing is prohibited from your direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No.,b:Yes.,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Crossing double solid yellow lines to pass is prohibited except for permitted turns into driveways or alleys.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Certain medications and drugs.,c:Lack of sleep.
note: Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness can all impair driving ability.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Braking distance,b:Reaction distance,c:Steering ability,d:Perception time
note: Stopping distance is based on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a direct factor.

question: If stopped by a police officer, what should you do while waiting?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,c:Get your paperwork out before the officer reaches the car.
note: Remain in the vehicle with hands visible, wait for the officer to approach and request documents; do not exit unless asked.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Drive around a lowered gate if traffic is light.,b:Speed up to cross before a gate comes down.,c:Look
note: Always look and listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop; never try to beat a train or bypass a gate.

question: What device is commonly used on highways to direct drivers into lanes for turning?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:Flashing yellow lights.,c:Lane arrows painted on the pavement.
note: Arrows on pavement or signs indicate which lanes are for turning or for through traffic.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are only used in construction zones,b:They are usually not important,c:They provide guidance and information for drivers
note: Pavement markings inform drivers about lane usage, passing zones, upcoming hazards, and correct positioning on the roadway.

question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren is approaching from behind?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Speed up to keep ahead of it.,c:Remain in your lane but slow down.
note: Yield the right-of-way: move to the right edge of the road and stop when safe to do so.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait for police to arrive before moving,b:Push it into oncoming traffic,c:Never move the vehicle,d:Move it off the traveled portion of the roadway
note: If possible after a minor collision, move your vehicle out of the travel lane to a safe location; do not leave the scene without providing required information.

question: If you need to slow on a slippery road, what should be your first action?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas.,b:Firmly apply your brakes.,c:Apply the parking brake.
note: On slippery surfaces, first remove your foot from the accelerator; if further slowing is needed, gently apply brakes.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver’s blind spot?
options: a:Flash your lights to alert them to your presence.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Avoid driving alongside large vehicles and do not tailgate.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots; avoid lingering beside them and maintain a safe following distance.

question: Which rule best describes passing other vehicles safely?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary,c:Try to reach the front of slow traffic to improve visibility
note: Pass only as needed and keep pace with the flow of traffic; excessive passing increases collision risk.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It allows turns without yielding.,b:It warns of a lane closure ahead.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular red light; you must stop and not turn in that direction.
note: A solid red arrow prohibits traffic in the direction indicated until the arrow changes.

question: On wet pavement, what conditions should drivers remember?
options: a:Wet roads have no effect on traction.,b:You can stop in the same distance as on dry pavement.,c:Pavement can be especially slippery right after rain begins and hydroplaning is possible.
note: Roads can be most slippery when rain first begins because oil and debris mix with water; slow down and increase stopping distance to avoid hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, who must you yield to?
options: a:Only bicyclists in the roundabout,b:Vehicles already in the roundabout,c:Only pedestrians in the roundabout
note: Yield to vehicles and bicyclists already circulating in the roundabout, and watch for pedestrians crossing the approaches.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the posted limit and impede traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Continue at the same slow speed,b:Pull off the road and allow others to pass,c:Refuse to let others pass,d:Increase your speed suddenly
note: If you're driving significantly slower than traffic on a two-lane road and causing backups, you must pull off and let others pass.

question: When entering a crowded freeway, how should you merge into traffic?
options: a:Enter at any speed and force your way into a gap.,b:Use the acceleration lane to match speed to freeway traffic,c:Stop at the end of the ramp then merge quickly.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate and match freeway speeds, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: If stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, which documents must you produce?
options: a:Driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance,b:Only your license,c:Only proof of registration,d:Only proof of insurance
note: When stopped you must produce your license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance upon request.

question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It is the same as a circular green and you may go straight,b:It applies only to buses,c:You may go only if accompanied by a green circle,d:Traffic in the indicated lane must turn in the arrow's direction and may proceed
note: A green arrow allows movement in the direction shown and requires that traffic in that lane turn as indicated.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass.,b:Drive as far to the right side of the road as is safe and stop.,c:Stop immediately in the middle of the road.
note: On two-lane or undivided roads, immediately move to the right and stop; do not stop within an intersection.

question: What colors are used on signs that indicate distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Black with white letters.,c:Red with white letters.
note: Destination and directional signs are green with white letters or symbols to indicate exits and distances.

question: On a divided multilane highway, how should you respond when you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop as quickly as you can in your lane.,c:Slow down
note: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle, slow, move to allow a clear path, and stop; do not attempt to outdrive the emergency vehicle.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Pay attention and obey all traffic signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Share the road and treat tracks like a regular street.,c:Drive around lowered crossing gates if no train is visible.
note: Always obey signals, never drive around lowered gates, and look both ways before turning across train tracks.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Opposing traffic and passing is allowed.,c:Traffic lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is permitted.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; dashed lines mean drivers next to them may pass when safe.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Safely pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Stop where you are.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching from behind, create a clear path by pulling over to the right and stopping when safe.

question: If a driver behind you is driving aggressively, what is the safest action?
options: a:Move out of their way and avoid eye contact,b:Speed up to get away,c:Stare at the driver to show displeasure,d:Brake sharply
note: If confronted by an aggressive driver, try to get out of their way, avoid eye contact, and avoid any gestures or escalation.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should a driver do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when children are present,b:Always stop whether a sign instructs or not,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop,d:Speed up to clear the area
note: When approaching a school crossing be alert for children and prepared to stop; yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: At night, which road user is the hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night compared to roadside objects or other vehicles; use extra caution and low-beam headlights.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using a siren or lights approaches, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.,b:Pull to the right and slow down without stopping.,c:Pull to the right and stop.
note: You must immediately move to the right edge of the roadway and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of at least:
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers age 21 or older, operating a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or higher is illegal.

question: Does drinking coffee reduce your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes — it decreases BAC.,b:Yes — it cancels the effect of alcohol.,c:No — it has no effect on BAC.
note: Drinking coffee does not lower blood alcohol concentration or make you sober; it may only help you feel more awake.

question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle (less than 25 mph).,b:The vehicle is an ambulance.,c:The vehicle is a school bus.
note: An orange reflective triangle signals a slow-moving vehicle such as farm equipment or certain trailers.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:15 feet.,b:20 feet.,c:30 feet.
note: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant to ensure emergency access.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not permitted.
note: A dashed yellow centerline separates opposite-flow traffic and allows passing when the way ahead is clear and safe.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Only when exiting an expressway.,b:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view or in poor weather.,c:When following a motorcycle in ideal conditions.
note: Increase following distance when behind large vehicles that impede your view, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when being tailgated.

question: What lane width entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Half the width of a lane.,c:Only the bicycle lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane just like other vehicles; do not crowd them when passing.

question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:School zones and school crossings.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate you are in a school zone; be extra alert for children and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross the lines?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:To pass another vehicle if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Only to make a left turn into or from an alley
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them to make permitted left turns or enter/exit driveways.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:Children are no longer present.,b:The beginning of a reduced speed area.,c:The reduced school-zone speed restriction has ended.
note: An 'End school zone' sign shows that the special reduced-speed school zone is finished.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best practice?
options: a:Proceed slowly until there's an opening,b:Accelerate on the ramp to match freeway speed and merge safely,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait,d:Turn on hazard lights until merged
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach freeway speed and merge smoothly; yield to traffic already on the freeway.

question: What helps you avoid emergency stops while driving in traffic?
options: a:Honk to make others aware of your presence,b:Stay in the right lane only,c:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead gives you time to react to hazards without abrupt emergency stops.

question: Another driver is trying to pass you. What is the proper response?
options: a:Pull off the road immediately.,b:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow a safe pass.
note: When another driver is passing, slow or adjust speed to create a safe gap so they can return to your lane easily; keep right.

question: When should you always signal?
options: a:Only on highways.,b:Only when turning left.,c:Changing lanes
note: Use turn signals whenever changing lanes, entering/exiting parking spaces, or pulling into traffic to communicate with others.

question: Downward-facing triangular signs are used to tell drivers to do what?
options: a:Indicate school zones.,b:Indicate construction zones.,c:Yield.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is used for yield signs; slow down and yield the right-of-way when you see one.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you allowed to exceed the posted speed limit?
options: a:When passing another vehicle.,b:At no time.,c:Where no police officers are present.
note: You must never exceed the posted speed limit; passing does not justify speeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely you should:
options: a:Signal and expect freeway traffic to yield,b:Stop at the ramp and wait for a gap,c:Signal,d:Slow to a crawl to check traffic
note: Signal and accelerate on the ramp to match freeway speed, yielding to traffic already on the freeway.

question: If you must drive in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed limit.
note: Use low beams (not high beams) in fog and turn on headlights when visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less; high beams reduce visibility in fog.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the sidewalk,b:Turn them sharply toward the curb,c:Turn your front wheels away from the curb,d:Keep them straight ahead
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so a roll will be stopped by the curb.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution through an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless a different speed is posted, what is the speed limit inside condominium complexes?
options: a:35 mph,b:25 mph,c:Follow the posted speed limit,d:45 mph
note: Unless a different speed limit is posted, the default limit in condominium complexes is 25 mph. Always obey posted signs if present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are making a left turn, who must you yield the right-of-way to first?
options: a:Oncoming traffic,b:Pedestrians only,c:Drivers already in the intersection,d:Vehicles behind you
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians and bicyclists already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with traffic moving in opposite directions, what is the correct use of the shared center lane?
options: a:To slow down or stop before making a left turn,b:As a through-traffic lane when traffic is slow,c:To pass other vehicles
note: The center lane is for making left turns from either direction; do not use it for passing or as a through lane.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles that are using their sirens or flashing lights by pulling over and stopping when safe.

question: What color are signs that typically indicate areas of public recreation?
options: a:Red,b:Brown,c:Green,d:Orange
note: Brown signs indicate cultural or historical sites and areas of public recreation.

question: How is defensive driving defined?
options: a:Driving aggressively to control traffic.,b:Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.,c:Being more dangerous than not driving defensively.
note: Defensive driving means adjusting your driving to conditions, your physical/emotional state, and the actions of others to reduce crash risk.

question: Using which device increases distracted driver crash risk the most?
options: a:Radio.,b:Cell phone.,c:CD player.
note: Using a cell phone (including hands-free) or other audio devices can be a dangerous distraction and increase crash risk.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Following other vehicles closely to reduce traffic flow.,b:Getting ahead of slow drivers by aggressive maneuvers.,c:Identifying hazardous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating and avoiding dangerous situations before they lead to a crash.

question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill grade, what should you know?
options: a:You are always permitted to safely pass it on the left.,b:The truck will match posted speed on hills.,c:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Large vehicles slow on inclines; exercise caution and do not attempt unsafe passes on hills with limited visibility.

question: What do orange-colored road signs typically indicate?
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:Construction
note: Orange signs are used for construction, maintenance, and emergency operations, usually with black symbols or words.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle immediately, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you actually see the vehicle.,b:Slow down but do not stop until you see it.,c:Pull to the curb and stop while you try to locate it.
note: If you hear an emergency vehicle nearby but don’t know its location, safely pull over to the right and stop until you can be sure it is not coming toward you.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge, how should you return to the road?
options: a:Speed up and steer quickly back onto the pavement.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to snap back onto the road.,c:Slow down gently
note: Ease off the gas, gently brake to reduce speed, and when safe, steer back onto the pavement—avoid sudden movements.

question: What must you do if you leave your vehicle unattended?
options: a:Turn off the engine only.,b:Set the parking brake only.,c:Turn off the engine
note: When leaving your vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: Which of the following statements is true about motorcycles?
options: a:It is okay for other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,b:A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than a single rider.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to full lane width; ensure you move fully into the adjacent lane before passing a motorcycle.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:If you are driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.,b:When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.,c:When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights; on a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop and remain stopped while red lights flash and/or the stop arm is extended.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition does not impair your driving?
options: a:Know the effects of any medicine on your driving ability,b:Be aware of your physical limitations and drive only when safe,c:Keep physically fit and get regular examinations
note: Be aware of how medicines and health conditions affect driving; know your limitations and seek medical advice or avoid driving when impaired.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light tell you to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Merging traffic.,c:Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should drive with caution.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect on either.,b:It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.,c:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, vision, judgment of speed/distance, and can lower inhibitions, making driving unsafe.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:At your rearview mirror,b:At your side mirror,c:Over your left shoulder,d:Over your right shoulder
note: Check the blind spot by glancing over the shoulder in the direction you intend to move.

question: If you see other drivers acting angrily or aggressively, how should you respond?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact and avoid them,b:React with hand gestures to show you won’t be intimidated,c:Distance yourself mentally and physically from the situation
note: When confronted by angry drivers, avoid eye contact and gestures and do what you can to put space between you and the aggressive driver.

question: How can you relieve fatigue during a long trip?
options: a:Drive with one eye closed to stay alert.,b:Stop and rest every two hours.,c:Do arm exercises while driving.
note: Schedule regular breaks—about every two hours—to rest and stretch to reduce fatigue on long trips.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean?
options: a:It is never used as a traffic signal.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.,c:It means drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is ending and you should slow and prepare for a red arrow.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous inside a vehicle?
options: a:It lowers fuel economy drastically.,b:It can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment.,c:It causes louder horn noise.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow carbon monoxide to build up inside the vehicle, which is poisonous and potentially fatal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition may you continue through an intersection showing a yellow light?
options: a:If there is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane,b:If pedestrians are crossing,c:If you were already in the intersection when the light turned yellow
note: If a steady yellow appears while you are already within the intersection, continue through it cautiously; do not stop abruptly.

question: What are the standard colors of warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:White letters or symbols on blue,b:Black letters or symbols on yellow,c:Black letters or symbols on white
note: Most warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols; work zone warnings are orange with black markings.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive through shallow water,b:Drive more quickly,c:Drive more slowly
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to help tires clear water from the road and avoid hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, where should you complete the turn?
options: a:Either lane,b:The lane closest to the direction you came from,c:The right lane
note: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you are coming from into the lane closest to that lane on the one-way street.

question: What should you do before switching on your ignition?
options: a:Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts,b:Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts,c:Buckle your safety belt and ensure all passengers are buckled
note: Develop a routine: before starting the engine, fasten your seat belt and confirm that all passengers are properly restrained.

question: What effect does increasing your vehicle’s speed have on your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It has no effect on your field of vision.,c:It decreases your field of vision.
note: Higher speeds narrow your effective field of vision, reducing your ability to see hazards in time to react.

question: What symbol indicates a slow-moving vehicle?
options: a:Rectangular red sign,b:Diamond-shaped yellow sign,c:Reflective orange triangle,d:Flashing blue light
note: Slow-moving vehicles display a reflective orange triangle indicating they travel 25 mph or less.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Back in without aligning,b:Turn wheels left immediately,c:Pull up even with the car in front of the space,d:Turn wheels right immediately
note: Before backing into a parallel parking space, stop parallel to the car ahead of the space to align your vehicle.

question: When should you reduce speed while driving?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads,b:Only when the road is wet,c:Only at intersections
note: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in blind curves, where there are pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

question: If a vehicle with ABS loses traction on a slippery road, how should you brake?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly,b:Press and hold the gas pedal,c:Pump the brakes
