note: With Anti-Lock Braking System, press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer to safety; ABS will modulate braking automatically.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a:Only if sirens are used,b:Only if it is approaching from behind,c:Only if it is following you,d:Whenever it approaches
note: You must pull to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights regardless of its direction of approach.

question: What is a "No zone" around a large vehicle?
options: a:A designated no passing zone.,b:A one-way traffic area.,c:The blind spot of a large vehicle.
note: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles; avoid lingering there to stay visible to the truck driver.

question: If you are involved in a crash and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Always leave the injured where they are without checking them.,b:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.,c:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.
note: Do not move injured persons unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if you are able while waiting for emergency responders.

question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicates what?
options: a:Always come to a full stop at the intersection,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians,c:Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is approaching
note: A triangular red-and-white sign is a yield sign; you must slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians, stopping if necessary.

question: How far ahead (in seconds) should drivers look down the road to help prevent sudden stops or turns?
options: a:5 seconds,b:12 seconds,c:10 seconds
note: Scan about 12 seconds ahead while driving to anticipate hazards and avoid abrupt maneuvers.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:A circle.,b:A rectangle.,c:An octagon (eight-sided).
note: Stop signs are uniquely octagonal. All eight-sided signs indicate you must stop completely before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.,b:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the light changes
note: A steady red requires you to stop. You may turn right on red after stopping unless a sign prohibits it and when it is safe to do so.

question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by which color lines?
options: a:Red,b:Yellow,c:White,d:Blue
note: Solid and broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; yellow separates opposite directions.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady braking while steering to safety,b:Shift to park immediately,c:Reach down and try to lift the pedal,d:Turn off the ignition while moving
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep control, shift to neutral, apply steady pressure on the brake, steer safely off the road, then turn off the engine.

question: Which is a safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter the curve and accelerate as you exit,b:Maintain the same speed throughout the curve,c:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and gradually accelerate as you exit to maintain control and traction.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They obey different traffic laws than cars.,b:They always have the right-of-way.,c:They can be harder to see and may move differently than larger vehicles.
note: Smaller road users can be more difficult to spot and have less visible lighting; always watch for them to prevent collisions.

question: How must you treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:You must obey them at all times.,b:They are merely suggestions.,c:Only follow them when other traffic is present.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control flow and safety and must always be obeyed.

question: When is it allowable to pass another vehicle on the shoulder?
options: a:Never — do not drive off the pavement to pass,b:When the vehicle ahead is turning,c:When there are no pedestrians present,d:When traffic is very slow
note: You may not drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass under any circumstances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The suggested speed under ideal conditions.,b:The maximum legal speed under dangerous conditions.,c:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed you may travel under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions are unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When passing is allowed,b:Always in construction zones,c:Only on rural roads,d:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic
note: Driving unreasonably slow so as to disrupt traffic flow is illegal; drive at a safe speed consistent with conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn approaching vehicles,b:Drive out quickly to merge with traffic,c:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway
note: When entering from a private road or driveway, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bike lanes?
options: a:Slow until there is no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving sufficient space.,b:Continue straight — the bicyclist must move.,c:Do not pass until a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but allow at least 3 feet (more on higher-speed roads) and avoid startling them with unnecessary honking.

question: Which statement about a work zone is true?
options: a:It is marked with black and white signs.,b:It does not require drivers to slow down.,c:It may be moving or stationary and requires extra caution.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving (e.g., line painting) and are marked by orange signs; slow down and pay attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on ordinary non-highway streets (not freeways or subdivisions)?
options: a:25 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:35 mph.
note: Unless a different limit is posted, the typical maximum on such roads is 55 mph in Michigan.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Excessive speed for conditions,c:Following other vehicles too closely,d:All of the above
note: Common causes of crashes include speeding for conditions, inattention, and following too closely; all contribute to accidents.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check blind spots?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Turning left or right.
note: Look over your shoulder to check blind spots whenever you change your vehicle's position, including changing lanes, turning, or curbing.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean?
options: a:You must stop and yield to oncoming traffic.,b:Passing is allowed only during daylight.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing in either direction except to turn where permitted.

question: If a green arrow at an intersection changes to a solid green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You may no longer turn in that direction.,b:You keep the right-of-way to turn without yielding.,c:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A solid green requires yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.
